tool.name: VS Code
tool.description: Visual Studio Code in the browser
tool.command: mkdir -p workspace/inputs && #import re #if $inputs and str($inputs) != 'None' #for $d in $inputs #set $name = re.sub('[^\w\-.]', '_', str($d.element_identifier)) #if not $name.endswith('.' + str($d.ext)) #set $name = $name + '.' + str($d.ext) #end if ln -sf '$d' 'workspace/inputs/$name' && #end for #end if export EP_PATH="\${EP_PATH:-/}" && exec /opt/galaxy-vscode/start.sh

param.name: inputs
param.label: Datasets to make available in the workspace
param.help: Linked read-only under workspace/inputs/. Save anything you want back in Galaxy under workspace/outputs/.

param.name: bucket
param.label: Google Cloud Storage bucket for Batch jobs
param.help: Optional, and only for Galaxy servers running on Google Cloud. Needed to send work to Google Cloud Batch with the batch command; job files are kept under galaxy-vscode/batch/ in this bucket. Give the bucket name, with or without gs://.

validator.message: Enter a bucket name such as my-bucket or gs://my-bucket

tool.help:
Launches Visual Studio Code (OpenVSCode Server) as a Galaxy Interactive Tool.
Selected datasets are linked read-only under ``workspace/inputs/``. Files saved under ``workspace/outputs/`` with a file extension (for example ``notes.txt``) are imported into your history as a collection when the tool is stopped.
The integrated terminal has ``python3`` with ``bioblend``, ``R`` with the language server and an IRkernel for notebooks, ``micromamba`` for conda packages, ``git`` and the Google Cloud CLI. ``GALAXY_URL``, ``API_KEY`` and ``HISTORY_ID`` are set, and ``galaxy-get <dataset>`` / ``galaxy-put <file>`` move data between the history and the workspace. ``batch run <command>`` sends a command to Google Cloud Batch, using the bucket named on this form. The workspace ``README.md`` has the details.
